title: Automating a process nobody understands
summary: Map real work, including its exceptions and informal decisions, before deciding what to automate.
diagnosis: A workflow diagram can be technically correct and operationally false. Work may actually pass through private spreadsheets, calls, queues and improvised interpretations. Some missing steps are undocumented knowledge; others are unresolved decisions about how the business should operate. Distinguish those two situations so that an engineer is not asked to invent policy while building an integration.
diagnostic_questions: Can a person follow one ordinary case and one difficult case from trigger to accepted completion?
Where does the work wait, change format, need clarification or rely on an unnamed expert?
Which steps are unnecessary, and which apparent inefficiencies protect quality, relationships or accountability?
proposed_actions: Observe real cases with frontline workers; capture inputs, transformations, handoffs, waits, decisions, exceptions and completion evidence.
Assign business owners to unresolved rules before implementation; distinguish historical practice from approved policy.
Redesign the smallest useful end-to-end slice, comparing elimination, simplification and automation rather than preserving every existing step.
working_artifact: Reality-based workflow map: trigger; input source; step owner; active effort; waiting time; decision rule; evidence; tool; exception route; approved outcome. Attach representative normal and difficult cases.
measures: End-to-end elapsed time and active touch time, reported separately for comparable case types.
Rework and clarification loops per completed case.
Fraction of consequential decisions with an agreed rule or explicitly owned judgement boundary.
tradeoff: Do not spend months documenting the entire company before trying anything. Map deeply enough to understand the chosen scope and its consequential dependencies. Do not remove a handoff merely because it is slow: first establish whether it serves a legitimate control or customer purpose.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: invoice matching takes minutes, but obtaining the correct contract and approving an exception takes days. Improving extraction alone may have little effect until the evidence and approval path are redesigned.
